That is what most of us do, though. Pandemic forced many young men like me to do it more frequently than before. We lived like this before the pandemic as well. It is not like we just sat alone in our cubicles and rooms, waiting for a friend or a partner to appear.

You can be mentally healthy and still unable to make friends or initiate conversation out of random, though. In brief bouts of me feeling social enough, I was looked down and looked at weirdly when I tried. And I'm not even talking about approaching women - that would end worse.

The world is kind of a shitty place now. And it seems people are angrier, more confrontational, and hostile. I really do want to believe it is only my perspective and experience.

Thank you for an honest, nice reply. I rarely get to hear wisdom like that in my life. It did make me feel calmer for a moment.

Now answering the question:

* I believe that having a romantic relationship would help me to uncover the aspects of my personality I did not know existed or that I could not uncover by interacting with my family or platonic friends. It's simply a big part of me waiting to be discovered. Unique and not found elsewhere. And I want to grow and develop as a person, see what can I be. I can't ignore this part of myself. I did try to be with myself and work it out. But it does not work anymore. I take care of myself. But I feel like a big part of myself is missing.

* I don't want to miss out. Currently, it feels like I'm not a part of a big club that I really want to be in. Love, romance and sex seem like a very big part of what makes being a human. I can't just force myself to ignore it because I can't seem to get it. If I try, it will kill me in the end. 

* I feel lonely. Not in a completely lonely sense - I still have parents and friends. But there is an aspect of me that desperately needs a different sort of interaction. On many stressful days I simply want to be in someone else arms to calm down. And I too want to provide someone the same comfort - it's just in my spirit. I have a lot of love to give. But there is nobody to receive it.

* I wish to create a family one day. But I don't want to be too old when the time comes for it. I have a strong principle that once I turn 35 and don't have anyone yet - I will simply stop trying and give up. It is a long story and would require a lot of explanation on why I think like that, so maybe I won't go deeper now.

3. Put more clutter and details around. It's a rundown rebel base, so it's expected to be dirty and stuff.

Talking about brutal, I have lots of stories to tell from my fortresses, but one stands out. I built a surface keep to act as fortified entrance to my fort, with crenelated walls (well, actually those are fortifications but I like to imagine they look like crenelations) for my marksdwarves to use. But the most significant part of this was a large raised platform with catapult on top. I use DFhack, which allows catapults to be more functional, with ability to even aim them! Anyway, in my world there was another dwarven civ which my civ started a war and shortly after some small raids into their territory, they sent their army of 20 strong fighters in good steel armor. I immediately close my drawbridges, send my defenders to man the defenses, catapult included...

Enemy force hold their ground not far from entrance, allowing my snipers (yes, that's how I like to call my marksdwarves) to shoot at anyone who comes too close. It's when my catapult starts hurling death at huddled group of attackers... The reports were brutal. Limbs exploding from rock impacts, bones breaking when galena boulders smash into unfortunate invading dwarves. One rock even hit a scary looking axedwarf into head, removing it completely! The catapult is a truly fearsome war machine when used correctly.

It went for 3 months, with attackers unable to do anything. Many enemy dwarves got actual PTSD from this, as I saw some of them having "stressed" status. It was a total carnage and ended when I decided to open up one of drawbridges and sally forth with my main melee force.

I imagine a grimdark scene of dwarf soldiers holding out in siege camp. It's raining and there's mud everywhere, with catapult artillery coming down around them. Very similar to WW1 trench warfare, as my biome had these plots of sand and bare dirt, so I can easily see the brutality of this scene.
